parts.solution_md:
> *Write the highest common factor of *$12y^{2}$* and *$-9y$* outside the bracket*

$3 y ( )$

> *Inside the bracket write what this needs to be multiplied by to give *$12y^{2}$* and *$-9y$

$3 y ( 4 y - 3 )$

**[M1 A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: Any correct factorisation. E.g. $y ( 12 y - 9 )$.
> 
> **A1**: Correct fully factorised answer.

> **[exam-tip]**
> In an exam, "factorise" means "fully factorise". This means using the highest common factor of the terms.

> *Multiply *$( x - 2 )$* by *$x$*, and add on *$( x - 2 )$* multiplied by *$7$

$x^{2}-2x+7x-14$

> *Simplify*

$x^{2}+5x-14$

**[B1 B1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **B1**: At least 2 terms correct.
> 
> **B1**: All 3 terms correct. Must be simplified.

parts.problem_md:
i) Multiply out the brackets.

$x ( 3 - 5 x )$

[2]

ii) Factorise fully.

$5x-20x^{2}$

[2]
parts.solution_md:
(i) *Multiply each term inside the brackets by *$x$*.*

> * *$\begin{gathered} x \times 3 & = 3 x \\ \\ x \times ( - 5 x ) & = - 5 x^{2} \end{gathered}$

> * Write together.*

$3x-5x^{2}$* ***[2]**

**one mark for each**

(ii) *The highest common factor of 5 and 20 is 5. The highest common factor of *$x$* and *$x^{2}$* is *$x$*. *

> *Take out a factor of *$5x$*. Divide each term by *$5x$* to work out what goes in the brackets. *

$5x$$(1-4x)$* ***[2]**

**one correct expansion*** ***[1]**

> *Write out the expressions with the *$m$* terms together and combine like terms. *

$8m-5m+12+10\,\,=3m+22$

* *$3m+22$* ***[1]**
